meta.purpose: Test whether colour beyond a functional floor adds useful scanning value. Holds chroma as low as WCAG floors and the distance matrix tolerate.
meta.tradeoffs: Lowest chromatic attention hypothesis; weakest categorical cue and smallest CVD headroom. Nominal area-weighted spectral output is evaluated separately and is not inferred from chroma. Diagnostics are deliberately exempt from the restraint.

must_distinguish.note: The CVD floor is lower than the normal-vision floor because we accept that a dichromat sees a *reduced* difference; we only require that the difference does not vanish.  Pairs that cannot meet this must carry a redundant channel, declared in roles.yaml.

non_goals.claim: Every syntax role gets a unique hue.
non_goals.reason: Produces rainbow highlighting, exhausts the perceptual budget, and degrades badly under CVD. We use ~5 hue families for ~14 syntax roles and spend the remainder on salience.
Most frequent token class, least informative distinction. Colouring them means the majority of chromatic pixels carry no information.

non_goals.claim: All pairwise distances should be maximised.
non_goals.reason: Distance is zero-sum inside a bounded gamut. Maximising everything flattens the semantic structure that the grouping above encodes.

non_goals.claim: Punctuation should match its enclosing construct.
non_goals.reason: Rainbow-bracket-style coding raises the noise floor across a major area class to disambiguate a structure that indentation already conveys.

cvd.note: dichromacy (severity 1.0) via Brettel 1997; anomaly (severity 0.6) via Machado 2009; tritan always Brettel. Population-average dichromat models; they detect collapse, they do not reproduce an individual's experience (RESEARCH.md R-9).

spectral.caveat: Exploratory nominal-display model; within-model ranking only. An sRGB triple does not determine a spectral power distribution; this never claims actual retinal exposure (RESEARCH.md R-4, R-5).

must_distinguish.note: The CVD floor is lower than the normal-vision floor because we accept that a dichromat sees a *reduced* difference; we only require that the difference does not vanish.  Pairs that cannot meet this must carry a redundant channel, declared in roles.yaml.

non_goals.claim: Every syntax role gets a unique hue.
non_goals.reason: Produces rainbow highlighting, exhausts the perceptual budget, and degrades badly under CVD. We use ~5 hue families for ~14 syntax roles and spend the remainder on salience.
Most frequent token class, least informative distinction. Colouring them means the majority of chromatic pixels carry no information.

non_goals.claim: All pairwise distances should be maximised.
non_goals.reason: Distance is zero-sum inside a bounded gamut. Maximising everything flattens the semantic structure that the grouping above encodes.

non_goals.claim: Punctuation should match its enclosing construct.
non_goals.reason: Rainbow-bracket-style coding raises the noise floor across a major area class to disambiguate a structure that indentation already conveys.

cvd.note: dichromacy (severity 1.0) via Brettel 1997; anomaly (severity 0.6) via Machado 2009; tritan always Brettel. Population-average dichromat models; they detect collapse, they do not reproduce an individual's experience (RESEARCH.md R-9).

spectral.caveat: Exploratory nominal-display model; within-model ranking only. An sRGB triple does not determine a spectral power distribution; this never claims actual retinal exposure (RESEARCH.md R-4, R-5).
